articles.title: The Chart Lesson Upstairs
articles.summary: A navigation student skips the knot room to catch an early berth, then must choose between his certificate and a lamp coming loose in the fog.
articles.summaryZh: 一名学生为赶上春汛前的船位跳过绳结课，却在雾中必须从证书和一盏松脱的信号灯之间作出选择。
storyParagraphs: At Grey Cape Navigation School, knots were taught downstairs and charts upstairs. Luan could already find a position from the stars and calculate the tide, and his uncle had promised him a paid berth if he earned his certificate before the spring floods. The ground-floor course would take a month. After looking at Luan's high entrance marks, the head instructor allowed him to go straight upstairs. Luan folded the exemption slip into the brass case of his compass and climbed the stairs before anyone could reconsider.

For several weeks, the shortcut seemed deserved. In tabletop exercises, assistants secured the model buoys while Luan drew routes through shoals and cross-currents. His charts were fast, clean, and usually first on the wall. During one harbour drill, a line he had wound around a cleat began to creep. The assistant caught it under his boot, retied it, and said nothing. Luan saw the rope burn across the man's glove, but the next bell was already calling the class back to the chart room.

The final test began before dawn. Fog had erased the practice channel, so each student had to take a cutter out and hang three signal lamps that would guide the following boats. The assistant who normally handled Luan's lines had been assigned elsewhere. Luan secured the first red lamp as he remembered seeing others do it. It held while the cutter idled. Once the sail filled, the knot slipped a finger's width, then another. Behind him, another student was already steering toward the red glow.

If Luan completed the course, the certificate was still possible. If he stopped the test, the spring berth would go to someone else. He pulled the wet rope around his wrist and tried to reach the next marker. The lamp swung lower; its reflection moved toward the pale water above the shoal. Luan took out his knife. He cut away the lamp, fired the return flare, and heard the examiner's whistle answer through the fog. The cutter behind turned in time, but the school's brass lamp vanished under the water.

On shore, Luan could have blamed the soaked rope. Instead he laid the loose end, the compass case, and the exemption slip on the examiner's table. The school charged him for the lost lamp and cancelled his test. His uncle's ship sailed three days later with another apprentice. While the mastheads passed beyond the cape, Luan carried his rolled chart down to the room he had skipped.

All month he tied lines with dry hands, then wet gloves, then with his eyes covered. On the morning of his second test, he fixed a red lamp to the practice rail and leaned back until the hemp tightened against the wood. Only when the rail shook did he unfold his chart beside it. The old exemption slip remained in the compass case, creased through the head instructor's signature.
storyParagraphsZh: 灰角航海学校的一楼教绳结，二楼教海图。陆安已经会看星位，也能把潮水算得很准。叔父答应，只要他在春汛前拿到证书，就给他一个有工钱的船位。一楼的基础课要花整整一个月。总教员看过陆安的入学成绩，准许他直接上楼。陆安把免修单折进黄铜罗盘盒，趁教员还没改变主意，抱着书跑上了楼梯。
最初几周，这条捷径像是他应得的。桌面演习时，助教替他绑好模型浮标，陆安只需在浅滩与横流之间画出航线。他的图又快又整齐，总被最先挂上墙。一次港内训练，他绕在羊角桩上的绳慢慢滑了出来。助教一脚踩住，重新系好，什么也没说。陆安看见粗麻绳在对方手套上磨出一道白痕，可楼上的钟已经响了。
结业考试在天亮前开始。浓雾抹掉了练习航道，学生要各驾一条小艇，挂出三盏信号灯，为后船标路。平日替陆安收紧绳索的助教被调去了别处。他照着记忆系好第一盏红灯。小艇未动时，绳结纹丝不动；帆一吃风，绳头先滑出一指，又滑出一指。身后的同学已经把船头对准那团红光。
继续走完航道，他还有机会拿到证书；停考，春汛前的船位就会给别人。陆安把湿绳在手腕上绕了一圈，仍想赶到第二个标记。红灯却越垂越低，水里的倒影正往浅滩的灰白处移。他抽出小刀，割断灯绳，又打出返航信号。雾里立刻响起考官的哨声。后船及时转向，学校那盏铜灯却沉进了水里。
回到岸上，陆安原本可以怪绳子受潮。他却把松开的绳头、罗盘盒和免修单一起放上考官的桌子。学校让他赔偿铜灯，并取消这次考试。三天后，叔父的船带着另一名学徒离港。桅杆越过海角时，陆安卷起那张满分海图，走进了自己跳过的一楼。
接下来的一个月，他先用干手系，再戴湿手套系，最后蒙住眼睛系。第二次考试那天清晨，陆安把一盏红灯固定在练习栏杆上，向后压下全身重量。麻绳贴紧木头，栏杆随之晃了一下。他这才把海图摊在旁边。那张免修单仍留在罗盘盒里，折痕正穿过总教员的签名。
explanationParagraphs: A prerequisite structure means that complex performance depends on foundational components that can be called upon reliably. Advanced work may look successful while teachers, tools, or familiar conditions quietly supply a missing foundation. The structure is not one rigid sequence for everyone, but essential knowledge or skill must be available when later tasks actually require it.
explanationParagraphsZh: 先备知识结构指复杂学习依赖若干能被稳定调用的基础成分。高阶表现有时看似成立，只因他人、工具或熟悉环境暗中补上了缺口。它并不要求所有人遵循完全相同的顺序，但当后续任务真正需要某项基础时，学习者必须能够独立使用它。

articles.title: The Apprentice Who Stayed After the Bell
articles.summary: A watchmaking student hides one unfinished skill to keep an apprenticeship, until the flaw is lifted into the town clock.
articles.summaryZh: 一名钟表学徒为保住作坊名额掩盖了尚未掌握的手艺，直到那处缺口被装进镇上的大钟。
storyParagraphs: The Seven Towns School of Horology had a rule that parents and workshops admired. Every sixth day, the courtyard bell rang and every apprentice moved to the next bench. The schedule told families exactly when fees would end and let workshops reserve graduates months ahead. Mira needed that certainty: North Street had offered her a place, but only if she finished before the master's son returned from sea. She kept the offer folded beneath the felt mat at her filing bench.

Mira could polish a pinion and set a spring, but she always filed one side of a gear tooth a shade too deep. On the sixth afternoon, her practice clock still lost time whenever a weight was attached. She tightened the spring until it ran correctly for the examiner's brief inspection. The bell rang. Her page received a blue stamp, and she crossed the courtyard with everyone else. That evening the empty clock on her old bench was already slowing again.

At the assembly bench, the weakness returned in larger pieces. A tower mechanism shuddered under load, and Mira quietly replaced her gear with one made by a classmate. Later, during a timed repair, a tooth caught hard enough to leave a bright nick on the steel. The instructor called it bad material. Mira held the North Street letter inside her apron and let him write another blue stamp beside her name.

Winter brought the school's public commission: repairing the town clock before market week. Mira's class fitted the mechanism while merchants waited below to reopen the square. Her gear turned smoothly without the bell weight. When the weight was hung, the uneven teeth struck one another. At noon the clock stopped, held its breath, then rang thirteen times. The school director ordered the face covered before the visiting guild masters arrived and told the apprentices to work through the night.

Mira found her first practice clock in the storeroom, its hands now twenty minutes late. If she kept quiet, the class could replace the damaged part and graduate on schedule. She carried the slow clock into the square and set it beneath the tower. Then she asked the director to remove every gear bearing her stamp. The clock missed market week, the school repaid the stall fees, and North Street gave her place to another graduate. For twelve days Mira remained alone at the filing bench while the courtyard bell sent each class onward.

She filed one tooth, tested it under weight, marked the error, and began again. On the thirteenth day, her practice clock kept time from dawn until the evening bell. Mira did not move when the courtyard rang. She waited for the instructor to hang the weight once more. Only after the hands completed another hour did she lift the North Street letter from beneath the felt and place the finished gear on top of it.
storyParagraphsZh: 七镇钟表学校有一条家长和作坊都喜欢的规矩：每隔六天，院钟一响，所有学徒便换到下一张工作台。家里能算准学费何时结束，作坊也能提前几个月预留新人。米拉尤其需要这份准时。北街作坊答应收她，条件是必须赶在师傅的儿子出海归来前毕业。那封聘用信一直压在她锉台的毡垫下面。
米拉会磨轴，也会调发条，唯独锉齿轮时总把一侧磨得稍深。第六天下午，她的练习钟一挂上砝码就会变慢。她把发条拧紧，让指针恰好撑过考官短短的检查。院钟响了，记录页盖上蓝章，她跟着众人穿过院子。当天夜里，旧桌上那只无人照看的钟又慢了下来。
到了组装台，这个缺口跟着零件一起变大。塔钟模型一受力就发颤，米拉悄悄换上同学做的齿轮；限时维修时，又有一枚齿卡出一道亮白伤口。教员说是钢料不好。米拉隔着围裙摸到那封北街来信，没有开口，让第二枚蓝章落在自己名字后面。
冬天，学校接下公开委托：赶在集市周前修好镇上的大钟。商贩等着钟声重开广场，行会师傅也会来验收。米拉做的齿轮在空转时很平顺，钟锤一挂上去，深浅不一的齿便彼此撞击。正午，大钟先停住，随后一口气敲了十三下。校长命人遮住钟面，要全班连夜换件。
米拉在库房找到第一只练习钟，它已慢了二十分钟。她若继续沉默，大家换掉坏件，仍能准时毕业。她却把慢钟抱到广场中央，请校长拆下所有带着她印记的齿轮。大钟错过集市周，学校赔了摊位费，北街也把名额给了别人。此后十二天，院钟每次催一批学生向前，米拉都独自留在锉台旁。
她锉一枚齿，挂上砝码检验，记下偏差，再从头来。第十三天，练习钟从清晨一直走到晚钟，没有慢下一分。院钟响时，米拉仍没有离桌。她等教员再次挂上砝码，看着指针完整走完一小时，才从毡垫下抽出那封已经失效的聘用信，把合格的齿轮放在上面。
explanationParagraphs: Mastery learning advances a learner after clearly defined outcomes have actually been reached, rather than treating equal time as equal learning. Evidence, specific feedback, correction, and another attempt keep small gaps from entering more complex work. Standards need not fall; what may vary is the path, support, and time required to meet them.
explanationParagraphsZh: 掌握学习依据学习者是否真正达到清晰目标决定下一步，而不把相同课时自动等同于学会。及时证据、具体反馈、针对性修正与再次尝试，可以阻止小缺口进入更复杂的任务。标准无需降低；可以变化的是学习路径、支持方式和达到标准所需的时间。

articles.title: The Bend That Wasn't on the Table
articles.summary: A prize-winning bridge apprentice brings his perfect model to a real river and discovers what the blue cloth never carried.
articles.summaryZh: 一名获奖的造桥学徒把完美模型带到真河边，才看见蓝布从未承载的东西。
storyParagraphs: Each year the Stonebridge Academy held a model contest. Blue cloth became a river, blocks became banks, and a measured stream from a copper jug tested the piers. Yizhen had won three years running. When the eastern bridge washed out, the mayor offered him the temporary crossing because grain merchants were threatening to take their trade elsewhere. If a cart crossed before the midsummer fair, the academy would give Yizhen a builder's seal. He arrived carrying his prize drawing in an oiled leather tube.

The drawing placed the main pier at midstream, where the load was balanced and the model current divided neatly. An old ferryman pointed upstream to a bend hidden behind reeds. In floodwater, he said, branches came sideways and struck the eastern bank. Yizhen unrolled the drawing on a flat stone. The academy had tested the design under three flow rates; moving the pier would waste both timber and the week already spent cutting joints. He ordered the crew to follow the centre line.

The first pier leaned overnight. Yizhen blamed loose gravel and drove the replacement deeper in the same place. It stood through two calm days, and the mayor announced an opening date. Then a moderate rise brought a raft of reeds around the unseen bend. They did not meet the bridge head-on as the model twigs had. They turned broadside, pressed against the centre pier, and snapped a guide rope. One worker escaped by dropping a basket of iron clamps into the river.

Only enough money remained to reinforce the centre pier or dismantle it and begin again. Reinforcement might save the opening date and Yizhen's seal. The ferryman dropped a peeled branch into the current. It travelled toward midstream, turned at the bend, and struck the wounded pier with its side. Yizhen followed another branch upstream, then found old water scars high on the eastern trees and broken reeds packed into the same crevices. His drawing had not been wrong on the table; the table had been missing the turn.

Before dawn, Yizhen told the crew to pull out his prize pier. The mayor withheld half the fee, the fair opened without a bridge, and Yizhen sold his brass drawing compass to replace the lost clamps. He shifted the span, angled it toward the arriving current, and added a sacrificial screen upstream to catch branches. The old ferryman made him test floating bundles at low and high water before the final deck went down.

The first grain cart crossed nine days late. Yizhen did not wait beside the mayor. He stood below the deck with one hand on the eastern brace while the wheels passed overhead. Back at the academy, he spread the award drawing on the blue cloth. Across its straight painted river, he laid the water-stained guide rope in a bend.
storyParagraphsZh: 石桥学院每年都办模型竞赛。蓝布是河，石块是岸，老师从铜壶里倒出定量的水，检验桥墩。易真连赢三年。镇东旧桥被洪水冲坏后，粮商正威胁改走别镇，镇长便把临时桥交给他：只要仲夏集市前能过第一辆车，学院就授予他正式工匠印。易真带着获奖图纸来了，图卷装在防水皮筒里。
图上主墩立在河心，受力均匀，模型水流也会从两边整齐分开。老艄公指着上游芦苇后看不见的急弯，说涨水时断枝会横着冲向东岸。易真把图纸摊在平石上。学院用三种流速试过这个方案；现在移墩，已经裁好的木料和一周工期都会作废。他还是命工人沿着图上的中线打桩。
第一根桥墩一夜便歪了。易真认定河底碎石太松，于是在原位把第二根打得更深。它撑过两个平静的日子，镇长随即公布了通桥日期。随后一次并不猛烈的涨水，把成片芦苇送出那道弯。芦苇没有像模型里的细枝一样正面穿过，而是突然横转，压住河心桥墩，还绷断了一根导索。一名工人把整篮铁箍丢进河里，才跳回岸上。
余钱只够选一件事：加固河心墩，或拆掉重来。加固或许还能保住开桥日和工匠印。老艄公削下一截枯枝，丢进水里。它先漂向河心，过弯后侧身撞上受伤的桥墩。易真又跟着一截树枝走到上游，在东岸树干上摸到高处的旧水痕，也看见石缝里塞着折断的芦苇。他的图在桌面上并没有算错，桌面只是少了这道弯。
天亮前，易真叫工人拔掉自己那根获奖桥墩。镇长扣下一半工钱，集市开张时仍没有桥，他还卖掉黄铜圆规，补回沉入河底的铁箍。新桥改成斜迎水流，上游多了一道可以替桥受撞的木栅。老艄公让他在低水和涨水时各放几捆树枝，确认它们的去向，才准铺最后一块桥板。
第一辆粮车晚了九天过桥。易真没有站在镇长旁边受贺，而是走到桥下，一手扶着东侧拉索，听车轮从头顶慢慢压过。回到学院，他把获奖图纸重新铺上蓝布，又把那根泡出水印的旧导索横放在笔直的河面上，摆成一道弯。
explanationParagraphs: Transfer of learning is the effective use of knowledge or skill in a situation different from the one in which it was learned. It requires recognising which underlying principles still apply and adjusting for changed conditions, not copying familiar steps. Contrasting cases, explaining why a method works, and practising when to use it all support transfer.
explanationParagraphsZh: 学习迁移是把一种情境中获得的知识或技能有效用于另一种情境。它要求识别哪些底层原理仍然成立，并依据新条件调整做法，而不是照搬熟悉步骤。比较多种案例、解释方法为何有效，以及练习判断何时使用，都有助于迁移发生。

articles.title: The Streets in a Different Hand
articles.summary: A delivery apprentice who memorises signboards as pictures loses the city when a new painter changes every hand.
articles.summaryZh: 一名把招牌当图画记忆的送信学徒，在新漆匠改写全城字迹后忽然失去了整座城市。
storyParagraphs: Eno wanted to leave the fish docks before winter and win a paid place at the post house. He could speak the traders' language but had only lately begun to read its alphabet. To prepare for the route test, he copied each street sign as a picture: the word for Salt Street curled like a fishhook; Bell Lane stood on three tall strokes; East Harbour ended in a blot shaped like a boot. When the tutor showed the same cards, Eno answered faster than anyone. He tied the bundle with blue thread and carried it on every practice round.

A week before the test, the city hired a new sign painter. Her letters were narrow, slanted, and joined where the old hand had left gaps. The fishhook disappeared; the three towers leaned together. On his first solo round, Eno carried a parcel for Bell Lane to the old bell tower. The postmaster deducted the return fare from his wages and warned that one more failed route would send him back to the docks. That night Eno did not change his method. He stayed up copying the new signs as new pictures.

The fresh cards helped the next morning, until he reached a shop whose owner had painted the address himself. None of the strokes matched. Eno compared the board with his bundle for so long that two noon letters missed the ferry. He began adding tiny drawings beside every unfamiliar hand: a bent nail, a ladder, a bird's foot. By week's end the bundle was thick enough to pull his coat pocket out of shape, yet every new writer seemed to require another picture.

On the test day, rain drove ink down the signs in grey threads. Eno had to carry the east warehouse key before the tide gate closed. At a fork, the painted shapes were almost gone. A baker's daughter beneath the awning sounded out the surviving marks one by one, joined them, and pointed left. Eno heard the spoken name he already knew. He looked again at the board and, for the first time, found the small mark that carried the first sound rather than the old fishhook around the whole word.

He reached the warehouse after the gate had shut. Instead of claiming that the storm made the test unfair, Eno returned the key and asked to sit the examination a month later. He lost four weeks of post-house wages. Each evening he separated words into sounds, matched those sounds to letters, and read the same names in the tutor's hand, the painter's hand, and hurried notes from shopkeepers. At first he whispered through every sign; gradually familiar written words came to him without searching for a picture card.

The second examination began with an envelope addressed in a hand he had never seen. Eno sounded out the unfamiliar name, delivered it, and came back by a street whose sign had been half repainted. He untied the blue thread from his old bundle. The fishhook card stayed in his pocket, folded once across the drawing.
storyParagraphsZh: 伊诺想在冬天前离开鱼码头，争到邮局一个有工钱的学徒位置。他会说外港商人的话，却刚开始认那套字母。准备路线考试时，他把每块路牌当成图画抄下来：盐街的词头像鱼钩，钟巷有三根高笔画，东港末尾的墨团像一只靴子。老师只要拿出同样的卡片，他总能第一个答对。伊诺用蓝线捆好卡片，每次练习都带在身上。
考试前一周，全城换了漆匠。新写的字又窄又斜，旧笔迹分开的地方也连在了一起。鱼钩消失了，三根高笔画挤成一排。伊诺第一次独自送件，就把钟巷的包裹送到了旧钟楼。邮局扣掉他的返程船费，还警告再错一次便让他回码头。当天夜里，伊诺没有换方法，只熬夜把所有新招牌重新画成一套新图。
第二天清晨，新卡片果然帮了忙，直到他遇见一块店主自己写的门牌。上面的笔画没有一处相同。伊诺站在门口翻了太久，两封午信错过渡船。他开始在陌生字迹旁加小画：弯钉、梯子、鸟爪。到周末，卡片已经厚得把外套口袋坠歪，可每出现一种新笔迹，他就得再添一张图。
正式考试那天下起大雨，路牌上的墨漆淌成灰线。伊诺必须在潮门关闭前，把仓库钥匙送到东港。岔路口的字形几乎全被冲花。面包店的小女孩站在屋檐下，把剩下的几个记号逐一读出声音，再连起来，指向左边。伊诺听见了自己熟悉的地名。他重新看那块牌，第一次寻找发出开头声音的小记号，而不是包住整词的旧鱼钩。
他赶到时，潮门已经落锁。伊诺没有说暴雨让考试不公平，而是交回钥匙，请求一个月后重考。他失去了四周的邮局工钱。此后每晚，他先把词拆成声音，再把声音和字母对应起来；同一个地名，要读老师的字、漆匠的字和店主匆忙写下的字。起初每块牌都得小声拼两遍，后来熟悉的词不必再去卡片里找图。
第二次考试，考官递来一封从未见过的笔迹。伊诺逐个读出字里的声音，把信送到，又沿一条只补漆了一半的街道返回。他解开旧卡片上的蓝线。那张画着鱼钩的卡片仍留在口袋里，只是从图案正中被折了一道。
explanationParagraphs: Orthographic mapping is the process by which a written word becomes linked in memory with its pronunciation and meaning. In alphabetic writing, successful decoding uses awareness of speech sounds and knowledge of letter-sound correspondences; repeated accurate encounters then support automatic recognition. It is not the visual memorisation of each whole word as one fixed picture.
explanationParagraphsZh: 正字法映射是书面词形与词语的发音、意义在记忆中建立稳定联系的过程。在字母文字中，读者依靠语音意识和字母—声音对应完成解码，并在反复准确识读后逐渐自动化，熟练后才能快速认词。它不同于把每个整词当成一幅固定图画死记。

articles.title: The Last Grain Boat
articles.summary: With floodwater entering the storehouse, a young worker must judge a boatload before the accountant can finish counting it.
articles.summaryZh: 洪水涌进粮仓时，一名年轻仓工必须在账房数完以前判断出最后一船的粮袋。
storyParagraphs: By the time the river covered the third stone step, the South Granary had one boat left. Its licence allowed up to 120 standard wheat sacks, and the boatman had to clear the bridge before the rising water closed the arch. The account book was soaked, so Clerk Gao crouched beside the stacks and began again at one. Qiao, the youngest warehouse worker, wanted a permanent post before winter; giving an order without the clerk's seal could cost her even the day work she had.

The sacks were normally stored ten to a row and twelve rows to a full bay. One bay now lacked two complete rows. In the side room, Qiao saw two loose groups that looked close to ten each. She said they could load the ten remaining rows from the bay and make up the last twenty from the side room. Gao had reached thirty-seven. Without an exact count, he refused to break the wax seals on the stack.

Water touched the lowest sacks. Qiao broke the first seal herself. To keep the pattern visible, she sent each pair of porters with one complete row and scratched a line on the door after every ten sacks. At the side room, the shortcut nearly failed: one heap that looked like ten held only eight because two sacks were lying crosswise behind it. Gao pointed to the gap and demanded they unload everything. The boatman loosened the stern rope; there was time for one correction, not a fresh count.

Qiao did not defend her first glance. She used a full row on the boat as a reference, split the side-room sacks into groups of five, and found two more beside the scale. Ten marked rows from the main bay made 100; four groups of five made twenty. She then assigned six porters to unload two rows each at the far bank, giving them a second way to check the total. Before boarding, she signed Gao's damaged ledger: any shortage would be deducted from her wages.

The boat cleared the bridge with its rail a hand's width below the stone. On high ground, the porters laid out twelve rows of ten. Gao counted every sack anyway and found 120. The grain was safe, but the broken seals still violated the granary rule. Qiao lost eight days' pay while the keeper reviewed what she had done. During the review, she still came to the high bank to help dry the sacks, but could not sign for wages. Her own wooden chest, left on the storeroom floor while she loaded, was ruined by the flood.

When the granary reopened, Qiao did not replace the swollen ledger with another long list. She painted ten spaces across the floor and twelve marks up the wall, then kept a separate square for loose sacks. The old door, cut above the waterline, still carried twelve knife scratches. She left the first one crooked.
storyParagraphsZh: 河水淹过第三级石阶时，南仓只剩最后一趟船。船证规定最多装一百二十只标准麦袋，水再涨，船就过不了桥洞。账册已经泡烂，高账房只好蹲在粮垛旁从第一袋重新数。最年轻的仓工小乔正盼着入冬前转成正式工；没有账房盖印就发粮，连眼下的零工都可能保不住。
粮袋平时十袋一排，十二排码满一格。眼前这格缺了两整排，侧屋另有两堆散粮，看起来各有十袋左右。小乔说，主仓剩下十排，再从侧屋补二十袋，正好一船。高账房才数到三十七，坚持没数清就不能拆粮垛上的蜡封。
水已经碰到最下面的粮袋。小乔亲手掰开第一枚蜡封。为了让数目看得见，她让每两名搬运工抬走完整一排，每过十袋就在门上刻一道线。到了侧屋，这个办法差点出了错：其中一堆看着像十袋，实际只有八袋，另外两袋横躺在后面。高账房指着空缺，要他们全部卸下重数。船老大却已松开船尾缆绳，只够改一次，来不及从头再来。
小乔没有替第一次目测辩解。她拿船上一整排作参照，把侧屋粮袋重新分成四组，每组五袋，又在秤台旁找到遗漏的两袋。主仓十排是一百，四组五袋是二十。她还约定靠岸后由六名搬运工各卸两排，再核一次总数。上船前，她在高账房泡皱的账页上签了名：若少一袋，就从她的工钱里扣。
船过桥洞时，船沿离石拱只剩一掌。到了高岸，搬运工把粮袋摆成十二排，每排十袋。高账房仍逐袋点完，恰好一百二十。粮是保住了，小乔擅自拆封却仍违反仓规。管仓人查了八天，她便少领八天工钱。复核期间，她每天仍来高岸帮忙晾晒粮袋，却不能签领工钱；留在侧屋地上的木箱，也在装船时被洪水泡坏了。
粮仓重开后，小乔没有照旧抄一长串袋号。她在地面横着画出十个位置，在墙上竖着留下十二格，旁边另画一格记录散袋。被锯下来保存的旧仓门上，仍有十二道刀痕。第一道刻得有些歪，她没有磨平。
explanationParagraphs: Number sense is a flexible grasp of quantity, magnitude, and numerical relationships. Benchmarks, grouping, decomposition, estimation, and more than one representation help a person judge what is plausible and choose an efficient calculation. It does not replace exact counting when precision is required; it guides action and provides independent checks.
explanationParagraphsZh: 数感是对数量、大小和数字关系的灵活理解。借助基准、分组、拆分、估计及不同表示方式，人能迅速判断结果是否合理，并选择有效算法。数感不替代需要时的精确计数；它为行动提供方向，也能用另一种方式核查答案，估计与精算应互相校验。

articles.title: The Man Who Could Read Every Notice
articles.summary: The port's finest reader can pronounce every line of a ferry notice, yet cannot use it to reach the right island.
articles.summaryZh: 港口最流利的朗读者能念出渡船告示上的每个字，却无法用它抵达正确的岛。
storyParagraphs: Jiang Wen had the finest hand in the harbour office. Whenever a new notice appeared, dockworkers asked him to read it aloud, and he never stumbled even over legal words. A permanent clerkship opened just as his mother's medicine bills rose. For the final trial he had to carry the winter labour register to East Island, obtain the overseer's seal, and return before sunset. He wrapped the register in oilcloth and chose his best brush to sign the delivery page.

At the ferry house, a large table listed islands, times, piers, market days, and tide symbols. Jiang Wen found 'East Island — eight o'clock' and went directly to Pier Two. He could pronounce the smaller line above it, but treated it as a heading that did not concern him. Halfway across, the ferryman explained that this boat went east only on market days. Today it would turn for West Bay. Jiang Wen read the relevant line aloud again, as if clearer pronunciation might change the route.

A vegetable seller beside him read slowly, following the date downward with one finger and the destination across with another. She also checked the black-moon mark, which sent low-tide passengers to Pier Four. At West Bay she transferred to a small boat and reached East Island before noon. Jiang Wen refused her offer to show him the table. He paid for the return ferry and hurried back to Pier Two, certain that the next eastbound entry must be the one he needed.

The second boat also turned away. Its line belonged to festival weeks, identified by a small lantern symbol in the corner. By the time Jiang Wen returned, only a private skiff could reach East Island before the office closed. He spent the money saved for his mother's next medicine order, but the falling tide exposed a mudbank and delayed the skiff. The island office shutter came down while he was still fifty paces away. He returned without the seal and lost the clerkship trial.

The next morning Jiang Wen asked the vegetable seller to meet him at the notice. This time he did not begin by reading from the top. He named the task, marked today's date, traced to East Island, checked the tide symbol, and then repeated the route to a ferryman. Over the following weeks he practised with cargo labels, medicine instructions, pay forms, and receipts, asking what decision each document was meant to support before sounding out every line.

When another register went to East Island in spring, Jiang Wen reached Pier Four before the gangplank dropped. He folded a copy of the timetable into a small square, leaving only today's row exposed, and clipped it beneath the delivery seal. His old calligraphy remained visible on the register. The crease across the ferry table was new.
storyParagraphsZh: 蒋闻是港务局里字写得最好的人。码头工人遇到新告示，总请他当众念一遍，连拗口的条文也从不停顿。恰逢局里空出一个正式文书名额，母亲的药费又在上涨。最后一项考核，是把冬季工人名册送到东岛，取得主管印章，再于日落前带回。他用油布包好名册，还带上最好的毛笔，准备在交接页签字。
渡口挂着一张大表，列着岛名、时间、码头、集市日和潮汐符号。蒋闻找到“东岛，八时”，直接去了二号码头。上方的小字他也能念，却认定那只是与自己无关的表头。船走到半程，船夫才告诉他：这班船只有集市日才去东岛，今天会转往西湾。蒋闻又把那一行响亮地念了一遍，仿佛读得更清楚，船便会改变方向。
同船卖菜的老妇人读得很慢。她先用手指沿日期向下，再顺着目的地横过去，还查了黑月记号——退潮时要从四号码头走。到了西湾，她换上一条小船，午前便到了东岛。她愿意教蒋闻怎么看表，蒋闻却谢绝了。他付钱坐船返回二号码头，认定下一条写着东岛的记录总不会错。
第二条船仍然转了方向。那一行只适用于节庆周，条件藏在角落的小灯符号里。蒋闻赶回渡口时，只剩私人小艇可能在办公处关门前抵达。他花掉原本留给母亲下次买药的钱，可退潮露出的泥滩拖慢了船。东岛办事处落下木窗时，他离岸边只剩五十步。名册没有盖章，文书考核也作废了。
第二天清晨，蒋闻请那位老妇人再到告示前见面。这回他没有从第一行开始念，而是先说清自己要办什么，找到当天日期，横向对到东岛，再核查潮汐符号，最后把路线复述给船夫。此后几周，他拿货签、药品用法、工资表和收据练习，每次先问这份文字要帮助人完成什么，再去辨认每一行。
春天又有一份名册要送东岛。栈桥尚未放下，蒋闻已经站在四号码头。他把时刻表副本折成一个小方块，只露出当天要用的那一行，夹在交接印下面。名册上仍是他原来那手漂亮字，渡船表上却多了一道新的折痕。
explanationParagraphs: Functional literacy is the ability to understand and use written language, numbers, tables, and symbols to complete real tasks. It includes locating relevant information, recognising a document's purpose, combining conditions, and checking a decision. Fluent pronunciation or elegant handwriting alone does not ensure that a timetable, form, contract, or instruction can be used.
explanationParagraphsZh: 功能性读写能力是理解并使用文字、数字、表格和符号完成现实任务的能力，包括定位相关信息、识别文件用途、组合条件并核查决定，还需要依任务调整阅读方式。朗读流利或书写漂亮，并不保证一个人会使用时刻表、表单、合同或操作说明。

articles.title: Three Lines at White Stone Fork
articles.summary: A courier who keeps buying better maps begins recording the decisions that lead him back to the same wrong road.
articles.summaryZh: 一名不断购买新地图的信使，开始记录那些把自己一次次带回同一条错路的判断。
storyParagraphs: Taosheng had one month left to earn the mountain courier's brass badge before snow closed the ridge. The test looked simple: deliver three parcels to Pinecrest Inn by dusk. On his first attempt he took the broad road at White-Stone Fork and returned to the foothills. He blamed an old map. On the second, he bought the newest edition in the market, followed the broad road again, and found the same charcoal kiln. The map seller offered a more expensive waterproof copy. Taosheng had money for either that or a pencil.

He bought the pencil. Into his existing map he folded a blank sheet and ruled three short lines: what he expected to see, what he actually saw, and how certain he felt. At each junction he stopped long enough to write. The notes irritated him. On the first afternoon they made him slower, and at White-Stone Fork he still chose the broad road because cart marks made it look safer. Twenty minutes later he reached fresh kiln smoke and had to turn back. He arrived at the inn after dark and lost his third examination fee.

That night, Taosheng laid all three attempts beside one another. The maps disagreed about small paths, but his own notes repeated a sentence: 'No signpost; broad road feels safer.' The road had not deceived him three different ways. He had used the same feeling as evidence each time. For the next attempt he added two marks to the sheet: a time by which each landmark should appear, and a box for what he would do if it did not.

On test morning, White-Stone Fork appeared under a crust of frost. His boots turned toward the broad road before he opened the notes. Taosheng stopped, read the repeated sentence, and chose the narrow path between low pines. Soon fog covered the ridge. The spring named on his map failed to appear by the time written on his sheet. Pressing on might save the badge; returning to the last certain point would cost nearly half an hour. He drew a cross in the box and went back.

Behind him, a fallen branch had hidden a small stone marker. From there Taosheng compared the slope on the map with the ground, changed to the lower path, and set a new checkpoint at the shepherd's wall. He reached the inn five minutes before dusk. The keeper stamped the parcel book but made no speech. Taosheng's page showed a crossed-out route, two revised times, and a smear where fog had wet the pencil.

On the return journey, the map seller held up a fresh edition in a leather cover. Taosheng still had no badge money to spare after paying the extra examination fee. He passed the maps and bought the thinnest notebook on the stall. Its first page carried the three headings from the folded sheet; beneath them, he copied the crooked cross from the ridge.
storyParagraphsZh: 陶生只剩一个月可以拿到山路信使的铜名牌，再晚，大雪就会封岭。考核看起来很简单：天黑前把三个包裹送到松岭客栈。第一次，他在白石岔口走上宽路，绕回山脚；他怪地图太旧。第二次，他买了集市上最新的版本，又顺着宽路走到同一座炭窑。地图商人还推荐一张更贵的防水图。陶生的钱只够买它，或买一支铅笔。
他买了铅笔，把一张空纸折进旧地图，划出三行：原本预计看见什么，实际看见什么，自己有多确定。每到路口，他都停下记一笔。这些字让人心烦，第一天下来还拖慢了脚程。到了白石岔口，他依旧因为宽路上有车辙，认定那里更安全。二十分钟后，前方冒出熟悉的炭烟，他只得折返。赶到客栈时天已黑，他又损失了一次考试费。
当夜，陶生把三次路线并排摊开。几张地图对小路的画法并不相同，他自己的记录却重复着同一句话：“没有路标，宽路看着更安全。”三次错误都出自同一个判断：他把“看起来更安全”当成了证据。第四次出发前，他又添了两项：每个地标最晚何时应当出现；如果没出现，下一步做什么。
考试清晨，白石岔口结着薄霜。陶生的靴尖已经转向宽路，他才翻开记录。看见那句重复三次的话后，他改走矮松之间的窄道。不久，浓雾盖住山脊。纸上写定的时间到了，地图标注的泉眼仍未出现。继续赶路或许能保住名牌；退回最后一个确认无误的位置，要损失将近半个时辰。陶生在应对栏里画了叉，转身往回走。
一根倒下的树枝遮住了来路旁的小石标。陶生从那里重新对照地图坡向和脚下地势，换走低处的路，又把牧羊墙设成下一个检查点。他在日落前五分钟抵达客栈。掌柜只在包裹簿上盖章，没有夸他。陶生的纸上留着一条划掉的路线、两个改过的时间，还有一块被雾水洇开的铅灰。
返程经过集市，地图商人举起一张带皮套的新图。陶生刚多付了一次考试费，口袋里没剩多少钱。他走过那些地图，买了摊上最薄的笔记本。第一页仍写着那三行标题；标题下面，他照着旧纸，抄下了山脊上那个歪斜的叉。
explanationParagraphs: Metacognitive regulation means planning an approach, monitoring understanding or progress, evaluating evidence and results, and adjusting strategy. Confidence, confusion, predictions, and outcomes become useful when they change the next action. It is not endless self-analysis; it is a timely check on whether the current method is working and what to do if it is not.
explanationParagraphsZh: 元认知调节包括计划方法、监控理解或进展、评价证据与结果，并据此调整策略。信心、困惑、预测和结果只有进入下一步行动才有价值。它不是无休止地分析自己，而是在关键时刻检查当前方法是否有效，并预先决定无效时怎样改变。

articles.title: The Seventh Landing
articles.summary: A lighthouse apprentice who no longer trusts her feet builds a record strong enough to carry her past the sixth landing.
articles.summaryZh: 一名不再相信自己双脚的灯塔学徒，用一页页完成记录把自己送过第六层平台。
storyParagraphs: Suying had worked below the lighthouse for half a year, mending shades, joining broken rope, and trimming wicks. The winter keeper's post would pay enough to keep her younger brother in school. But the post required climbing to the seventh landing alone. Months earlier she had slipped on the open stair at the third level. She caught the rail, yet ever since, the first gust tightened her knees. Other keepers told her to be brave. Their confidence only made her more careful not to look up.

The old keeper stopped encouraging her. He handed Suying a small oil can and entered one task in the duty book: second landing, calm weather. She delivered it and wrote the date herself. Two days later she went to the fourth level to replace a pane. On the next attempt, a gust rattled the stair before she reached it. Suying came down without the glass, and the old keeper simply left that line blank. She had evidence of one success and one unfinished climb, not a verdict on the whole tower.

The work rose by pieces. She carried dry rope to the fifth landing, first with the keeper below, then without him. She practised fastening her tool belt until she could do it with cold fingers. At the sixth landing, she learned to stop against the wall, breathe until she could feel both feet, and decide whether the next step was safe. Every return went into the duty book: height, wind, task completed, and where she had turned back. Oil spots spread across the pages.

A week before appointments were decided, the old keeper offered her an indoor storehouse job. It paid less but required no seventh landing. If she refused and failed the tower test, both posts would be filled by winter. Suying kept the offer overnight, then crossed it out in the morning. Her final task was to inspect the top lamp during an ordinary coastal wind, with the keeper waiting below but forbidden to climb for her.

At the sixth landing, the wind pulled one fastening loose and her spanner slipped from the belt. It struck the steps twice and fell into the grass. Calling the keeper would end the test; continuing meant completing the repair with the spare tool in the lamp room. Suying pressed the duty book against the wall. The earlier pages showed second, fourth, fifth, and sixth, including the day she had turned back. She closed it, checked the remaining buckle, and climbed the last flight. At the top she tightened the lamp catch and wiped salt from the glass.

Suying received the winter post, though her first month's pay was reduced to replace the lost spanner. In the duty book she wrote 'seventh landing' and the date, then left it open until the ink dried. The wind lifted the corner of the page, revealing the old blank line underneath. She placed the empty spanner loop across it as a paperweight.
storyParagraphsZh: 苏盈在灯塔下做了半年学徒，会修灯罩、接断绳，也会剪灯芯。冬季守塔人的工钱足够让弟弟继续上学，可这份差事要求她独自登到第七层。几个月前，她在三层露天楼梯上滑过一跤，虽然抓住栏杆，此后每逢第一阵海风，膝盖便会发紧。其他守塔人总叫她勇敢一点。别人越有信心，她越不敢抬头。
老守塔人不再劝。他递给苏盈一小罐灯油，只在值班簿上写了一项：晴风，二层。她送到后亲手记下日期。两天后，她去四层换玻璃；下一次，楼梯尚未走完，一阵风便摇响铁栏。苏盈抱着玻璃退了回来，老人只让那一行空着。簿上留下的是一次完成和一次中止，还不是整座塔给她下的结论。
任务一层层增加。她把晒干的绳送到五层，先让老人等在下方，后来独自去。她反复扣紧工具带，直到手指冻僵也能操作。到了六层，她学会贴墙停住，等自己重新感觉到两只脚，再判断下一步是否安全。每次回来，她都记录高度、风力、做完的事和退回的位置。值班簿的纸页渐渐沾满灯油。
守塔人选定前一周，老人给她另一个选择：留在室内管库房，工钱少些，却不用上七层。她若拒绝又没通过登塔考试，入冬时两份差事都会交给别人。苏盈把聘用单留了一夜，清晨在上面画了叉。最后的任务是在普通海风中检查顶灯；老人会等在塔下，却不能代她上去。
走到六层，一阵风扯松了工具扣，扳手从腰带滑出，在台阶上撞了两声，落进草地。叫老人来，考核便结束；继续上去，只能用灯室里的备用工具。苏盈把值班簿抵在墙上。前几页依次写着二层、四层、五层、六层，也留着她曾退回的那一天。她合上簿子，检查剩下的扣带，走完最后一段楼梯，在顶层拧紧灯扣，又擦掉玻璃上的盐雾。
苏盈拿到了冬季差事，第一个月的工钱却要扣掉一部分，赔偿丢失的扳手。她在值班簿上写下“第七层”和日期，墨迹干透以前一直没有合上。海风掀起纸角，露出下面那行旧空白。她把腰带上空着的扳手环压在了上面。
explanationParagraphs: Self-efficacy is a person's belief that they can organise and carry out the actions required for a particular task. It influences choice, effort, persistence, and recovery after setbacks. It is not general confidence and does not replace real competence. Credible mastery experiences, suitable modelling, feedback, and interpretation of stress can strengthen it.
explanationParagraphsZh: 自我效能感是人对自己能否组织并完成某项具体任务所需行动的信念，会影响选择、努力、坚持和受挫后的恢复。它不等于泛泛自信，也不能替代真实能力。逐步获得的成功经验、合适示范、反馈以及对紧张反应的解释，能为这种信念提供依据。

articles.title: The Four Bars Applause Always Covered
articles.titleZh: 总被掌声盖住的四小节
articles.summary: An inn violinist can charm a room by rushing past his weakest passage, until an audition begins exactly there.
articles.summaryZh: 一名客栈琴手总能用热闹结尾掩过最弱的乐段，直到一场考试偏偏从那里开始。
storyParagraphs: Haian played the same dance tune each night at the Riverside Inn. He knew where the tables would stamp along and where the final flourish would bring coins into the bowl. Only four bars in the middle resisted him: his left hand rushed ahead of the bow during a string crossing. Whenever the notes blurred, he accelerated into the familiar ending. The applause arrived before anyone could examine the mistake. With the inn due to close for repairs, Haian needed a place in the city orchestra to keep paying for his room.

He prepared by performing the whole piece twice every morning. The opening grew brighter and the ending faster, while the middle remained a narrow patch he crossed without looking down. At the audition, the examiner opened Haian's score to that patch and asked him to begin there. By the second attempt his fingers were already chasing the bow. The examiner stopped him, circled four places in red, and handed the score back. There was no applause to carry him into the next page.

The next morning the inn did not hear the full dance. Haian slowed the first string crossing until he could distinguish both notes, then repeated it only while the sound stayed clean. A drummer tapped three different tempos. When the error returned, Haian stopped at the exact beat, marked whether the bow or finger arrived first, rested, and began again. His practice sounded worse from the dining room: fragments, pauses, and the same two notes scraped dozens of times.

Guests complained, and the innkeeper told him to practise elsewhere or lose his attic room. Haian moved to an unheated storeroom by the river. After ten days his hand ached and the red circles still gathered around one shift. He first tried doubling the hours, but the mistakes multiplied as his attention thinned. He shortened the sessions, asked the drummer to signal only the missed beat, and tested the passage at a slightly faster tempo only after three clean attempts. The notebook beside his stand began to show fewer red strokes.

A wedding party then offered him enough money to cover a month's rent if he played all night on the eve of the second audition. The familiar dance would earn easy applause, but his hand would arrive tired. Haian refused and surrendered his room deposit instead. At the audition, the examiner again began with the four bars. Haian did not rush the crossing or hide the pause between bow and finger. When the last difficult note settled, the examiner turned to the next page.

That evening the Riverside guests called for the old dance. Haian played it through, and the middle passed without changing speed. The applause sounded no louder than before. Afterward he opened a new score, found the passage he could not yet play, and folded a small corner beside it. The old audition page, with four faded red circles, remained under the stand.
storyParagraphsZh: 海安每晚都在河边客栈拉同一首舞曲。他知道哪一段会让酒桌跟着跺脚，也知道热闹的结尾何时能把铜钱引进琴盒。只有中间四小节始终不听话：换弦时，左手总赶在弓子前面。声音一乱，他便加快速度滑进熟悉的结尾，掌声会在别人来得及细听前响起。客栈即将停业修缮，海安必须考进城里乐团，才能继续付房钱。
他每天清晨把整首曲子拉两遍。开头越来越亮，结尾越来越快，中间那一小段却仍像窄桥，他总低头冲过去。考试时，考官偏偏把谱翻到那里，让他直接开始。第二遍还没拉完，手指已经追着弓子跑。考官叫停，在谱上圈出四处红记号，把纸还给他。没有掌声替他带到下一页。
第二天，客栈里不再响起完整舞曲。海安把第一次换弦放得很慢，直到两个音都能分清，只在声音干净时才重复。鼓手替他敲出三种速度；错误一出现，海安便停在那一拍，记下是弓先到还是手指先到，休息片刻，再从原处开始。餐厅里听见的反而更难听：碎片、停顿，还有两个音被来回刮了几十次。
客人开始抱怨，店主让他另找地方，否则收回阁楼房间。海安只好搬到河边没有炉火的储物间。十天后，手开始疼，红圈仍集中在同一次移指。他先把练习时间加倍，疲倦时错误却更多。于是他缩短每轮时间，只让鼓手指出漏掉的那一拍；连续三次拉准后，才稍微提速。谱架旁的本子上，红记号终于一天天减少。
第二次考试前夜，一场婚宴请他通宵演奏，报酬足够付一个月房租。那首熟悉的舞曲会换来轻松掌声，可第二天上场时，手也会疲惫。海安拒绝了婚宴，也赔掉了客栈房间的押金。考官仍从那四小节开始。他没有抢快，也没有藏起弓与手指之间的间隙。最后一个难音落稳后，考官翻到了下一页。
当晚，河边客人又点那首旧舞曲。海安从头拉到尾，中间没有突然加速，掌声却并不比从前更响。散场后，他打开一份新谱，找到自己暂时拉不好的乐段，在旁边折起一个小角。那张留着四个褪色红圈的旧谱，仍压在谱架下面。
explanationParagraphs: Deliberate practice targets a clearly identified weakness with focused effort, informative feedback, correction, and repeated attempts just beyond current reliable performance. It differs from repeating an entire familiar routine, which may preserve fluency while hiding errors. Its exact form varies by domain, and rest, coaching, motivation, and opportunity also shape improvement.
explanationParagraphsZh: 刻意练习针对明确的薄弱成分，以集中注意、可用反馈、错误修正和略高于当前稳定水平的反复尝试促成改进。它不同于不断重复整套熟悉表现；后者可能维持流畅，却继续掩盖错误。具体做法因领域而异，休息、指导、动机和机会也会影响进步。

articles.title: The Channel on the Blackboard
articles.summary: A student who can reproduce the teacher's perfect canal must decide what to erase when real water refuses her drawing.
articles.summaryZh: 一名能默画标准水渠的学生，在真实的水拒绝照图流动时，必须决定擦掉什么。
storyParagraphs: At Greenfield School, every pupil could draw a drainage canal from memory. The teacher made two banks on the board, added one straight descending arrow, and the class copied it. Anning's pages were so exact that the village committee asked her group to drain the school garden before spring rains. If the beds stayed dry, each pupil could take home part of the onion harvest. Anning planted her family's row closest to the wall and carried her highest-scoring drawing in her apron.

She stretched a string through the centre of the garden and told the others to dig beneath it. The first bucket travelled several paces, then settled into a shallow pool. Anning compared the ditch with her page and decided it was too narrow. They widened it before lunch. The second bucket spread into the broader hollow, overflowed, and flattened six onion shoots. Her drawing was still clean. Their boots were not.

The teacher did not put a corrected canal on the board. He brought stakes, string, transparent tubing, and three basins. One pupil insisted the garden fell south because the wall looked lower there; another pointed east, where the water had actually stopped. They made small channels in trays, lifted one end by a finger, and watched the direction change. Then they marked water levels at different stakes. The taut string that looked level to the eye crossed two places where the ground rose.

Anning redrew the route around the hidden hollow. A test bucket reached the outlet, and the class cheered too soon. That night a steady rain filled the new channel faster than their bucket had. Water cut through the soft inner bank and ran toward the onion bed. To lead it into the old ditch beyond the wall, the channel needed a wider bend exactly where Anning's family row stood. Anning pressed one wet onion leaf between her fingers, then marked her family's row for pulling before the next rain.

Anning pressed her scoring sheet into the mud so the wind would not take it, then dug up her own onions. The class measured again, deepened the outlet, packed the outer bank, and tested several jugs at once. The next rain bent through the empty row and left the remaining beds standing. Anning took home no onions that season. In the classroom, her group placed their muddy stakes beside the blackboard drawing rather than replacing one fixed diagram with another.

At the end of term, the teacher returned Anning's old perfect page. A brown thumbprint covered part of the straight arrow. She erased the rest, drew the route they had built through the missing onion row, and wrote the measured heights at each turn. A few dried roots remained caught in the fold.
storyParagraphsZh: 青禾学校的学生都能默画排水渠。老师在黑板上画两道岸，再添一支笔直向下的箭头，全班照样抄进本子。安宁的图最整齐，村委会便请她带同学赶在春雨前排干学校菜园。只要菜畦不积水，每个孩子都能分到一份葱带回家。安宁把自家的那一排种在靠墙处，围裙里还装着那张满分页。
她从菜园中央拉起一根直绳，让大家沿线挖沟。第一桶水走了几步，便停在一处浅洼。安宁对照图纸，认定沟太窄，午饭前便叫人把它拓宽。第二桶水在更宽的低处摊开，漫出沟沿，压倒了六棵葱苗。她的图仍然干净，所有人的靴子却沾满了泥。
老师没有在黑板上重画正确答案，只带来木桩、细绳、透明水管和三只浅盆。有人坚持菜园向南倾斜，因为那边的墙看着更低；也有人指着东边，说水明明停在那里。他们先在盆里挖小渠，把一端垫高一指，看水怎样改向；再把水位逐点标上木桩。眼睛看着很平的那根绳，实际跨过了两处微微隆起的地面。
安宁据此把水渠改成绕过浅洼。一桶试水顺利到了出口，大家高兴得太早。当夜连下几个时辰的雨，流量远大于水桶，水切开新渠松软的内岸，又朝葱畦涌去。若要把它引进墙外旧沟，弯道必须扩大，位置恰好穿过安宁家那一排葱。安宁捏着一片湿葱叶，最后在自家那排插下木签：下一场雨前拔掉，今年她便没有收成带回家。
安宁把评分纸按进泥里，免得被风吹走，随后亲手拔起那排葱。大家重新测高，挖深出口，压实外岸，又同时倒入几壶水试验。下一场雨沿着空出的地面转弯，剩下的菜畦都站住了。那一季，安宁没有葱可带回家。回到教室，他们把沾泥的木桩放到黑板旁，而没有再用另一张固定图替换旧图。
学期末，老师把原来的满分页还给安宁。一枚褐色拇指印盖住了直箭头的一段。她擦掉余下的直线，照着菜园里穿过空葱畦的路线重画，并在每个转弯旁写下测得的高度。纸页折缝里，还夹着几根晒干的细根。
explanationParagraphs: Constructivist learning treats understanding as something learners actively build and revise by relating prior ideas to experience, evidence, language, and other viewpoints. Accurate reproduction does not guarantee a changed internal model. Teachers remain active: they design tasks, provide materials, question interpretations, and guide reflection without simply doing the thinking for learners.
explanationParagraphsZh: 建构主义学习认为，理解由学习者把原有观念与经验、证据、语言及他人观点联系起来，并在冲突中主动修正。正确复述不代表内部理解已经改变。教师并非退出，而是通过任务、材料、追问和反馈，让原有想法显现并获得重组。

articles.title: Before the Kiln
articles.summary: A pottery school can identify every failed bowl, but its red tags arrive only after the clay can no longer answer.
articles.summaryZh: 一所陶艺学校能准确找出每只坏碗，可红签总在泥土无法改变之后才到来。
storyParagraphs: White River Pottery School judged only finished work. After each firing, examiners tapped the rims, inspected the glaze, and tied red tags to rejected bowls. The system was orderly: everyone faced the same test, arguments were rare, and the kiln never waited for a hesitant apprentice. Xiaohe needed six approved bowls to join the guild stall at the autumn fair. Clay, glaze, and firing fees had already consumed nearly all the money her family had lent her.

Three firings gave her the same red note: rim too thin. Each time Xiaohe began another bowl, she could not tell how the wet rim differed from the one before. She made the fourth slightly heavier. It looked strong, but after firing it received a new tag: wall uneven. The examiner's judgement was accurate. It also arrived when the only possible correction was a hammer. Four red strings accumulated around the handle of her tool box.

Before the next firing, Teacher Lin stopped beside Xiaohe's turning wheel and touched one place on the fresh rim. The clay folded inward under a finger. Lin did not repair it or assign a mark. She cut an old rejected bowl in half, left a thickness gauge on the table, and asked Xiaohe where she would check the new wall before deciding it was ready. Xiaohe measured three points, added clay to one, and wrote her next action on a small paper slip.

The fifth bowl held its shape, but another apprentice's wide platter cracked while drying. Soon everyone crowded around Lin for a touch and a slip, treating the table as a new inspection queue. Work slowed, and pupils began waiting to be told what to fix. Lin removed his own pen. Each apprentice now had to leave the wet piece with two notes: the evidence they had checked and the change they intended to try. A partner could ask a question, but could not issue a grade.

On the last day before the fair firing, Xiaohe's sixth bowl looked the best she had made. One measurement near the base still felt uncertain. If she cut it open, she would miss the six-bowl quota and lose the guild stall; if she fired it, the hidden weakness might fail after sale. Xiaohe drew a wire through the bowl. The base was thin on one side. She surrendered her fair place, rebuilt the piece, and paid for a later firing with two days' wages from loading clay.

The rebuilt bowl came out sound. The examiner tapped it, recorded the final result, and left off the red tag. Xiaohe untied the four old red strings from her tool box. She kept the small pre-firing slip instead, rubbing away the dried streak of clay with her thumb until only the words 'check the base' remained.
storyParagraphsZh: 白河陶艺学校只评烧好的作品。每次开窑，考官敲碗沿、看釉色，再给不合格的碗系上红签。这个办法整齐而公平：所有人面对同一标准，很少争执，窑也不必等某个犹豫的学徒。小禾需要六只合格的碗，才能进入秋季行会集市。家里借给她的钱，几乎已经花在泥、釉和烧窑费上。
连续三次开窑，她都收到同一句红签：碗口太薄。可每次重新拉坯，小禾仍看不出眼前的湿碗和上一只有什么不同。第四只，她特意做得更厚；烧成后，它换来另一张红签：碗壁不匀。考官判断得很准，可信息到达时，能用的修正工具只剩锤子。四根红绳渐渐缠满她的工具箱把手。
下一炉前，林老师停在小禾的转盘旁，用指尖碰了碰刚拉好的碗沿。湿泥立刻向内塌下一块。他没有替她修，也没有打分，只切开一只旧坏碗，把测厚尺留在桌上，问她准备检查哪些地方，再决定是否入窑。小禾量了三点，在一处补泥，又把下一步写在一张短签上。
第五只碗撑住了，可另一个学徒的大盘在阴干时开裂。很快，所有人都排队等林老师来碰一下、写一张签，矮桌变成了新的考场。活慢下来，学生也开始等别人告诉自己怎么改。林老师收起自己的笔。此后每只湿坯旁必须由学徒写两件事：检查到了什么，下一步打算怎样试；同伴可以追问，却不能给分。
集市前最后一次烧窑，小禾的第六只碗看起来最漂亮，靠近碗底的一次测量却仍让她不安。切开检查，她便凑不满六只，失去行会摊位；直接入窑，藏着的薄处可能在卖出后开裂。小禾把切线穿过碗身。碗底一侧果然很薄。她放弃集市名额，重新做坯，又去搬了两天陶土，才挣到下一炉的费用。
重做的碗出窑后，考官敲过碗沿，记下最终结果，没有系红签。小禾把工具箱上的四根旧红绳一一解下，却留下了入窑前那张短签。她用拇指抹掉上面干透的泥痕，最后只剩“检查碗底”四个字。
explanationParagraphs: Formative assessment elicits evidence while learning can still change and uses it to decide the next teaching or learning action. Its value lies not in frequent scoring but in timely, specific, usable feedback and learner response. Final assessment can judge an outcome; information that arrives after revision is impossible cannot improve the process that produced it.
explanationParagraphsZh: 形成性评价是在学习仍可改变时取得证据，并用它决定下一步教学或学习行动。关键不在频繁打分，而在反馈是否及时、具体、可用，以及学习者是否据此采取行动。终结性评价可以判断结果；若信息到达时已无法修正，就难以改善产生该结果的学习过程。

articles.title: Seven Orders for the North Gate
articles.summary: A probationary messenger accepts seven spoken errands at once and carries the smallest ones while losing the gate.
articles.summaryZh: 一名试用信使一口气接下七道口头命令，记住了零碎小事，却把整座北门丢在脑后。
storyParagraphs: On Ajiu's first day as a probationary castle messenger, sixty grain carts were approaching the north gate before rain. A permanent place would let him move his father out of a damp cellar, so when the captain gave seven orders at once, Ajiu did not ask him to repeat them. He had to take a key to the stable, tell the kitchen to leave one stove cold, deliver separate letters to the east and west towers, change the north-gate flag, open its side entrance, and record the cart total. He repeated all seven while running.

At the kitchen, the cook asked which stove to leave cold. Ajiu could remember 'one fewer' but not whether it was the bread or soup fire, so he guessed. At the east tower, he delivered the right letter, then tucked the west-tower message into the cart ledger without noticing. Each new question pushed an earlier phrase aside. He kept rehearsing the flag colour and lost the instruction about the side entrance; then a stable boy called after him, and the colour disappeared too.

By the time Ajiu reached the north wall, carts were backed up to the river bridge. The old flag still flew, the side gate was barred, and rain had begun darkening the flour sacks. He could pretend the guard had missed an order and rush onward, but a wrong flag might send the convoy to the lower gate, where the arch was too narrow. Ajiu turned back to the captain and admitted that he no longer knew which instructions remained. The delay cost him that day's pay, yet the convoy was stopped before taking the wrong road.

The captain opened his own order book and found the seven items scattered across two pages. The same convoy would return the following morning. He grouped the tasks by place on a small card: stable on one line, kitchen on one line, the two towers on another, and the three connected gate actions together. The required flag colour was drawn beside the gate line, and the cart count received an empty box. Ajiu carried the card on a cord instead of carrying every unfinished sentence in his head.

At each stop, he exposed only the current line and crossed it out when the action was complete. At the towers, the two letters stayed under the same clip until both had been delivered. Before the north gate, Ajiu no longer rehearsed the stable and kitchen. He looked at one group: blue flag, side entrance, blank count. The gate was open when the first cart arrived. As each ten carts passed, he made one mark, then added the six groups.

After the sixtieth cart entered, Ajiu wrote the total in the box. He had still carried seven orders, but the card had held what did not need to occupy the same moment. The captain restored his day's pay only after the probation month ended. Ajiu kept the used card; one long line crossed it from the stable at the top to the filled square at the bottom.
storyParagraphsZh: 阿久成为城堡试用信使的第一天，六十辆粮车正赶在雨前驶向北门。拿到正式差事，他就能让父亲搬出潮湿的地窖。队长一口气交代七件事时，他没敢请对方重复：给马房送钥匙，提醒厨房少生一炉火，把两封信分送东西塔，再去北门换旗、开侧门、记下车数。阿久边跑边把七件事从头默念。
到了厨房，厨娘追问该少生面包炉还是汤炉。阿久只记得“少一炉”，便猜了一个。东塔的信送对了，西塔那封却在匆忙中被夹进车数账。每个新问题都把前一句往外挤。他反复背旗子的颜色，忘了要开侧门；马房学徒又在背后叫住他，旗子的颜色也随之消失。
等阿久跑到北墙，粮车已经排到河桥，旧旗仍在杆顶，侧门紧闭，雨点把面粉袋洇出深色。他可以说守门人漏听命令，再继续跑；可若旗子换错，车队会被引去拱门过窄的下门。阿久转身回到队长面前，承认自己已经分不清哪些事尚未完成。延误让他被扣掉当天工钱，却也在车队走错路前把它拦住了。
队长翻开自己的命令簿，才发现七件事散在两页上。第二天，同一批粮车还会来。他把任务按地点写在一张小卡上：马房一行，厨房一行，双塔一行，北门的三项连在一行。所需旗色直接画在旁边，车数则留出空格。阿久把卡片系在腕上，不再让所有未完成的句子同时挤在脑中。
每到一处，他只露出当前一行，办完便划掉。两封塔楼信压在同一只纸夹下，直到东西塔都送完才取下。走向北门前，阿久不再背马房和厨房，只看同一组里的蓝旗、侧门和空格。第一辆粮车到达时，侧门已经打开。每过十辆，他就在空格旁画一道线，最后把六组相加。
第六十辆车进城后，阿久把总数写进方格。他仍然完成了七道命令，只是卡片替他保管了不必同时占住心思的部分。直到试用月结束，队长才把那天的工钱补给他。阿久留下了用过的小卡，从顶端的马房到最下方填满的方格，一道长线穿过所有任务。
explanationParagraphs: Cognitive load theory starts from the limited capacity of working memory when information is unfamiliar. Task complexity, confusing presentation, and too many elements held at once can consume attention needed for performance. Sequencing, grouping related steps, external records, and established knowledge structures reduce avoidable load; they do not remove the inherent difficulty of the task itself.
explanationParagraphsZh: 认知负荷理论以工作记忆处理陌生信息的容量有限为起点。任务本身的复杂度、混乱呈现和同时保留过多要素，会挤占完成任务所需的注意。分步、把相关动作组块化、使用外部记录及调用已有知识结构，可以减少可避免的负担，却不会消除任务本身固有的难度。

articles.title: The Market Beneath the Mulberry Tree
articles.summary: A teacher makes the children's pebble market orderly enough for inspection and watches every customer disappear.
articles.summaryZh: 一位老师把孩子们的石子市场整理得足以接受检查，也眼看着所有顾客从市场里消失。
storyParagraphs: The children opened a market beneath the mulberry tree. Pebbles were coins, leaves were fish, and broken pieces of wood served as scales. When one seller raised a price, customers crossed the roots to another stall. Children without enough pebbles pooled their money for one large 'fish', then argued about how to divide it. Teacher Lin had been asked to demonstrate early mathematics when the district inspector visited the following week. She stood nearby with a notebook, listening as three children disputed whether a torn leaf was worth three pebbles or four.

Lin feared the inspector would see only dirt and make-believe. She spent two evenings printing identical paper coins, price cards, role badges, and a worksheet with ten sums. On Monday she assigned every child a stall, fixed every fish at five coins, and rang a handbell for buying and selling. The market looked orderly at once. The first worksheet boxes filled quickly because all exchanges used the same number. Lin could point to written answers. The children no longer needed to bargain.

By the third bell, one seller had stacked his five-coin fish and stopped speaking. Two buyers discovered that choosing between stalls made no difference. A child who had invented delivery by wheelbarrow was told to remain the cashier. Within fifteen minutes, a ball rolled along the wall and most of the market ran after it. Lin rang again. Only the price cards answered in the wind. The next day she offered stickers for completed sums; the children returned for the stickers, finished the sheet, and left before the shade moved.

With four days until the visit, Lin crossed the tidy rehearsal off her timetable and left the lesson unfinished. She put the badges and paper coins away. Under the tree she left empty boxes of different sizes, chalk, string, several baskets, and one real balance scale. When the children returned, she did not restore the old market for them. One found that the largest wooden fish would not fit its box. Two sellers wanted the same scale. Another marked a delivery route, then discovered that a tree root blocked the cart. Prices, schedules, measurements, and rules reappeared because the market needed them.

On inspection day, Lin abandoned the prepared demonstration. One child was explaining why two small leaves could trade for one large leaf; another lowered a chalk price because the neighbouring stall had attracted every buyer. A quarrel over the scale stopped both stalls. Lin asked, 'What could let each shop use it before closing?' Then she stepped back. The inspector's form noted that the planned ten sums had not been completed. Lin did not receive the teaching commendation she had hoped would secure a transfer closer to home.

After the market closed, Lin found the unused worksheet beneath the scale. On its blank reverse, she recorded the children's plan to build two delivery carts and test which boxes stayed on them around the root. A purple mulberry had been crushed across the printed sums. She let the stain dry before placing the page in tomorrow's tray.
storyParagraphsZh: 孩子们在桑树下开了一座市场。石子是钱，树叶是鱼，断木片是秤。有人涨价，客人便跨过树根去另一摊；钱不够时，几个孩子会合伙买一条“大鱼”，再为怎样分它争起来。区里的督学下周来访，要求林老师展示早期数学学习。她拿着本子站在旁边，听见三个孩子为一片撕开的叶子究竟值三颗还是四颗石子争了很久。
林老师担心督学只看见泥土和假装游戏。她连续两晚印出一样大小的纸钱、写好的价牌、角色胸牌和十道算术题。星期一，她替每个孩子分配摊位，把所有鱼定价五枚，还用手铃规定买卖时间。市场立刻变整齐了。因为每次交换都是同一个数，练习格很快填满，她也有答案可以展示。孩子们不再需要讨价还价。
第三次铃响后，一个卖家把五枚一组的鱼叠好，便无话可说；两个买家发现去哪一摊都没有差别。原本想出手推车送货的孩子，被要求继续坐着收钱。不到一刻钟，一只球沿墙滚过，多数人便追着它离开。林老师再次摇铃，风里只有价牌晃动。第二天，她用贴纸奖励做完题的人，孩子们回来拿走贴纸，写完就走，连树荫都没移动多少。
离督学来访只剩四天，林老师却把整齐排练从日程上划掉，让那堂课重新变得未完成。她收起胸牌和纸钱，只在树下留下大小不同的空盒、粉笔、细绳、几只篮子和一把真正的天平。孩子们自己回来，她没有替他们恢复旧市场。有人发现最大的木头鱼装不进盒子；两个卖家抢同一把秤；另一个孩子画出送货路线，却被凸起的树根挡住。价钱、时间、测量和规则，因为市场确实需要，再次被他们拿起来。
督学来时，林老师放弃了准备好的展示。一个孩子正解释为何两片小叶可以换一片大叶，另一个在地上降价，因为隔壁摊吸引走了所有客人。两摊又为天平争执，谁也无法继续卖。林老师只问：“关市以前，怎样让两家都用上它？”随后退到一旁。督学表上写着“预定十道算式未完成”。林老师没拿到原本希望凭借这节课争取的优秀评语，也没能调去离家更近的园所。
散市后，林老师在天平底下找到那张没用过的练习表。她翻到背面，记下孩子们明天想造两辆送货车，并试一试哪些盒子绕过树根时不会掉下来。一颗紫桑葚正好压烂在印好的算式上。她等污迹干透，把纸放进了第二天的材料盘。
explanationParagraphs: Play-based learning uses active, meaningful, socially interactive, repeatable, and often imaginative play as a setting for learning. Adults deliberately arrange materials, time, questions, and suitable challenge, but do not replace children's consequential choices with a scripted exercise. It is neither unstructured abandonment nor gamification through points and rewards.
explanationParagraphsZh: 游戏本位学习把儿童主动、有意义、可互动、可反复尝试且常含想象的游戏作为学习情境。成人会有意识地安排材料、时间、问题和适度挑战，却不以脚本练习取代儿童真正有后果的选择。它既不是放任不管，也不是用积分与奖励包装任务的游戏化。

articles.title: The Nest Beyond the Picture Cards
articles.summary: A teacher keeps bringing a child back to her picture cards until she follows his finger toward the eaves.
articles.summaryZh: 一名老师不断把孩子带回自己的图卡，直到她顺着他的手指看向屋檐。
storyParagraphs: Before a supervision visit, Teacher Xu prepared twenty animal picture cards. Her contract review required a recorded language session, and she hoped Xiaomo would say five new words on camera. He knew the routine: sit opposite, look at a card, repeat the name. Yet halfway through each set he turned toward the window. Xu moved the cards into his line of sight and sometimes gently straightened his shoulders. He looked at her briefly, then returned to the same patch of roof beyond the glass.

During the first recording, Xu showed a bird card and asked three times for the word. Xiaomo pointed past it. The timer ran out with only two responses. Xu scheduled another session and moved the table so the window was behind him. He stopped pointing, but he also stopped offering words. When she raised the bird card, he pushed it face down. The second video looked quieter and more orderly than the first; it contained less between them.

That afternoon, while preparing a third attempt, Xu heard a dry scrape at the eaves. Xiaomo had found the window again. His finger aimed at a bundle of grass beneath the roof, where two small birds carried twigs in and out. Xu lowered the card, walked beside him, and followed the line of his hand. She waited. When one bird returned, Xiaomo looked from the nest to Xu's face, then pointed again as if checking that she had seen the same arrival.

'Nest,' Xu said, looking toward it. Xiaomo watched the bird disappear into the grass, glanced back at her, and made an unclear version of the word. Xu did not ask him to repeat it for the camera. Over the next few days they returned when the birds were active. She placed the picture cards on the windowsill. Sometimes Xiaomo looked at the real bird and searched for its card; sometimes he tapped the card and waited until Xu turned with him. Their attention travelled out and back.

On supervision day, Xu left the table against the wall and submitted a session that no longer followed her written plan. She placed two chairs side by side at the window, with the cards between them. Xiaomo pointed when a bird landed. Xu followed, named it, and waited; he looked back before touching the matching card. The supervisor postponed Xu's contract score because the original target had not been tested. Xu accepted another review month rather than pull his face toward the camera.

A week later, wind loosened one twig from the nest. Xiaomo saw it fall, touched Xu's sleeve, and pointed down. She looked with him before either spoke. On the sill, the old bird card had curled in the sun. Xu set a smooth stone on one corner and left the space between their two chairs open toward the window.
storyParagraphsZh: 督导来访前，许老师准备了二十张动物图卡。续约考核要求提交一段语言活动录像，她希望小默能在镜头前说出五个新词。流程本来很清楚：面对面坐好，看卡片，跟着念名字。可每次翻到一半，小默就转向窗外。许老师把卡片移到他的视线里，有时轻轻扶正肩膀。他会看她一瞬，很快又望向玻璃外同一块屋顶。
第一次录像时，许老师举起鸟的图卡，连续问了三遍。小默却越过卡片指向后面。计时结束，只录到两个回答。她另约一次，把桌子转过去，让窗户留在小默背后。他不再指了，也不再主动发出词语。许老师举起鸟卡时，他把卡片按倒。第二段录像比第一段安静、整齐，两个人之间发生的事却更少。
那天下午，许老师准备第三次活动，忽然听见屋檐上传来细碎刮擦声。小默又找到了窗户，手指对着檐下的一团枯草，两只小鸟正叼着细枝进出。许老师放下卡片，走到他身边，顺着手指看过去，没有立刻说话。一只鸟飞回来时，小默先看鸟巢，又回头看她，再指一次，像在确认她是否也看见了同一件事。
“巢。”许老师望着屋檐说。小默看着鸟钻进草团，又看了她一眼，轻声说出一个不太清楚的“巢”。许老师没有要求他对镜头重说。接下来几天，他们总在鸟儿活动时回到窗边。图卡被放在窗台上。小默有时先看真鸟，再寻找对应卡片；有时先点卡片，等许老师和他一起转向窗外。两人的目光在物与人之间来回走。
督导当天，许老师让桌子继续靠墙，提交了一段已经偏离教案、也没有收齐五个目标词的活动。她把两把椅子并排放在窗边，图卡留在中间。鸟落下时，小默伸手指，许老师跟着看、说出名字，然后等待；他回头看她，再碰了碰相应卡片。因为原定目标没有按计划测完，督导暂缓了许老师的续约评分。她接受多一个月观察，也没有把小默的脸转向镜头。
一周后，风从鸟巢上吹落一根细枝。小默看见了，轻碰许老师的衣袖，又指向窗下。她先和他一起望过去，两个人都没有急着说话。窗台上的旧鸟卡已被阳光晒得卷角。许老师拿一颗光滑石子压住它，把两把小椅子之间的位置继续朝窗外空着。
explanationParagraphs: Joint attention occurs when two people coordinate attention toward an object or event and recognise that the focus is shared. Pointing, following another's gaze or gesture, alternating looks between person and object, and a timely response can support language and social communication. Forced eye contact or merely looking at the same thing does not by itself establish shared attention.
explanationParagraphsZh: 共同注意发生在两个人把注意协调到同一对象或事件，并彼此意识到焦点共享时。指向、跟随目光或手势、在人与物之间来回查看及及时回应，都能支持语言与社会沟通。强迫目光接触，或两人恰好看着同一物体，并不必然构成共同注意。

articles.title: After It Rained During Shape Week
articles.summary: A storm carries a teacher's planned shape lesson into the yard, where the children's questions gather at a drain.
articles.summaryZh: 一场雨把老师准备好的形状课带进院子，孩子们的问题则一起聚到了排水口。
storyParagraphs: Teacher Zhou had prepared Shape Week for a month. Circles, squares, and triangles covered the tables, and the headteacher would observe on Friday before deciding whether Zhou's probation was complete. On Monday morning heavy rain crossed the yard. A child's paper boat floated around a puddle and vanished into the drain beside the wall. The class gathered at the grating, asking where the boat would go, why all the water chose that opening, and why the round hole did not immediately clog with leaves.

Zhou called them inside three times. She began the planned sorting game, but the children placed the paper shapes in a row leading toward the door. One drew the missing boat inside a circle. Zhou finished the first activity and could have dismissed the distraction. Instead she wrote down their questions and watched the grating at the next break. The same children returned, and new ones tested twigs and leaves in the shallow stream. The interest had survived more than the excitement of the storm.

On Tuesday, Zhou brought clear tubing, water jugs, chalk, strainers, and blocks of different shapes into the yard. She marked a dry boundary so no one reached into the real drain. The children traced water paths, built model inlets, and poured equal jugs. A solid square block stopped the flow; a triangular frame let water through but caught broad leaves; one large round hole emptied faster until a flat leaf covered it. Zhou photographed each version and wrote beside it what the builders predicted before the pour.

The work created its own trouble. Children kept changing several parts at once, then argued about which change made the water faster. One group flooded another group's chalk map. Zhou did not simply follow every new idea. She limited each test to one changed feature, gave different children roles in pouring, timing, and drawing, and brought books showing where drains lead. By Thursday, the original shape cards had returned as labels for openings and frames, but they no longer supplied the answer in advance.

On Friday the headteacher expected the rehearsed table lesson. Zhou left the class beside the drain and carried an inquiry with no known ending into her evaluation. She handed over the original plan, then the week's questions, predictions, drawings, and revised models. The children were debating whether to enlarge one circular opening or add three smaller ones. Zhou's probation was extended for a month because the planned objectives had not been assessed in the promised form. She accepted the delay and scheduled a separate check of the shape knowledge the project had not made visible.

After school, Zhou found the original paper boat caught safely in a maintenance basket beyond the grating. She dried it beside the unused shape cards. On Monday she placed the children's final drain drawing on top, added the boat at the corner, and rewrote the first line of the next plan: 'Begin with what we still need to find out.' The rain mark remained across the old Friday schedule.
storyParagraphsZh: 周老师为“形状周”准备了整整一个月。桌上铺满圆形、方形和三角形卡片，园长将在周五听课，再决定她能否结束试用期。星期一清晨，大雨横扫院子。一个孩子的纸船绕过水洼，被吸进墙边排水口。全班围上去，接连问：船会到哪里？水为什么都往这个口流？圆洞为什么没有立刻被叶子堵住？
周老师叫了三次，才把他们带回室内。预定的形状分类开始后，孩子们却把纸片排成一条通往门口的路，还有人在圆形里画那只消失的船。她做完第一项活动，原本可以把这当作雨后的兴奋。课间，她却带着本子再去排水口观察。原来那批孩子仍在，新加入的人还把细枝和叶片放进浅水。问题没有随暴雨一起过去。
星期二，院子里多了透明水管、水壶、粉笔、滤网和不同形状的积木。周老师划出安全界线，不让孩子把手伸进真排水口。他们沿地面描水路，搭出模型入口，再倒入等量的水。实心方块会截住水；有空隙的三角架让水通过，却拦住宽叶；一个大圆孔起初排得快，直到一片平叶把它完全盖住。每次倒水前，周老师都先记下建造者的猜测。
探究也带来了新的麻烦。孩子们常一次改好几个地方，随后争不清究竟哪项变化让水更快；一组倒出的水还冲掉了另一组的粉笔图。周老师没有追随每个突然冒出的主意。她规定每轮只改一个条件，让不同孩子分别负责倒水、计时和画图，还带来介绍排水去向的图书。到星期四，原来的形状卡重新出现，成了孔洞和框架的标签，却不再预先给出答案。
星期五，园长期待那节排练好的桌面课。周老师让孩子继续留在排水沟边，把这场尚不知道结尾的探究带进了自己的评分。她先递出旧教案，再拿出一周的问题、预测、图画和改过的模型。孩子们正争论该扩大一个圆孔，还是增加三个小孔。由于原定目标没有按承诺形式完成评估，周老师的试用期被延长一个月。她接受延期，并另约时间检查这次活动尚未显露的形状知识。
放学后，周老师在格栅后的清理篮里找到了那只纸船。她把它和未用完的形状卡一起晾干。星期一，她将孩子们最后的排水口图放在卡片最上面，把纸船夹在一角，重新写下新计划的第一行：“先从我们还需要弄清的事开始。”旧的周五安排上，仍横着一道雨水印。
explanationParagraphs: Emergent curriculum develops from children's sustained interests, questions, and working theories. Teachers document what they notice, judge its learning potential, and intentionally add materials, knowledge, participation structures, and assessment. It is not improvised aimlessness or following every passing preference; professional goals and children's inquiry are brought into a responsive plan.
explanationParagraphsZh: 生成课程从儿童持续表现出的兴趣、问题和初步解释出发。教师通过观察记录判断其学习潜力，再有意识地加入材料、知识、参与安排与评价。它不是随意发挥，也不是追随每个短暂偏好，而是让专业教育目标与儿童真实探究共同进入可调整的计划。
